name: transactions
description: A MUTATE block is one transaction, not a script that happens to run in order: everything in it commits or none of it does. A precondition that fails leaves the element exactly as the caller last saw it, and the two guards ask different questions — EXPECT VERSION about what the caller read, EXPECT STATE about the engine state, which is not an Assertion's epistemic status.

cases.name: a clause that fails undoes the clauses that already ran beside it
so the clause that succeeded left nothing behind
a stale EXPECT VERSION refuses the write
cases.command: UPSERT CONCEPT ?p { MATCH {key: "person:alice"} EXPECT VERSION 99 SET FIELDS {name: "Rewritten"} }

cases.name: and the refused write changed nothing
a selection block that matches nothing is a no-op, not an error
cases.command: UPDATE ?c SET ATTRIBUTES { note: "unreachable" } WHERE { ?c CONCEPT {name: "Nobody"} }

cases.name: EXPECT STATE on a retraction asks about the claim's standing, and refuses when it does not hold
cases.command: RETRACT ASSERTION ?a WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} } EXPECT STATE "retracted"

cases.name: the claim it refused to touch is still active
a guard that holds lets the withdrawal through
cases.command: RETRACT ASSERTION ?a WHERE { ?a ASSERTION {} } EXPECT STATE "active"

cases.name: and the claim is withdrawn rather than deleted
